key_insight: V-PaSS improves prediction for unfamiliar perovskite solar cells by representing absorber alloys and device stacks through physically informed, chemically meaningful features.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support screening of new absorber compositions and transport-layer combinations without requiring a pre-solved crystal structure for every alloy.
method: Interpolate relaxed crystal graphs from 23 pure ABX₃ endpoints using Vegard’s law and learned bandgap bowing.
Encode layer sequence, cell polarity, and interfacial band offsets.
Represent chemical descriptions with a scientific language model.
evidence_signal: On institution-grouped tests with unseen laboratories, untuned V-PaSS achieved 2.861% MAE versus 3.017% for a gradient-boosted baseline, with reported error reductions of 15.7–19.0% on unseen absorber alloys.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the 23-endpoint representation and the reported benchmark distributions remains to be established.
paper_title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
